title: Aiptasia Spawning and Embryo/Larvae Handling
author: OSU Weis Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rbsd2ne

steps.title: Maintain low‑density polyp cultures
steps.instruction: Place no more than 3–4 Aiptasia polyps in a Cambro 92CW plastic food container (17.6 × 10.8 cm) and keep at 25 °C under a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle with white light intensity of 15–20 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Feed polyps and monitor growth
steps.instruction: Feed dense cultures of brine shrimp at least five days per week and change the water at least every other day; continue this regimen until polyps reach an oral‑disk diameter of ~0.5 cm, then transfer them to the spawning incubator while maintaining the same feeding and water‑change schedule.

steps.title: Configure spawning incubator lunar cycle
steps.instruction: Program the incubator to provide blue light (peak 450 nm) at ~10 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹ during the 12 h dark period for the first five days of each 28‑day cycle; expect spawning to occur between days 13–20, usually within the first two cycles if polyps are well fed and healthy.

steps.title: Set up male‑female crosses
steps.instruction: If precise fertilization timing is required, keep male and female polyps in separate containers; otherwise, mix sexes in the same container. Note that gamete release typically occurs ~6 h after the onset of darkness.

steps.title: Collect eggs and sperm with mesh screens
steps.instruction: Use appropriate mesh screens to separate gametes: pour water containing sperm from male‑only tanks through a fine mesh (e.g., < 100 µm) to remove debris, and pass eggs through a larger mesh (e.g., 100 µm) to filter debris. Eggs are ~80 µm in diameter, round, white, and opaque; sperm may be observed as cloudiness in the water.

steps.title: Fertilize eggs in culture dish
steps.instruction: Mix the collected eggs and sperm in a 1 500 mL (8‑inch) glass culture dish (Carolina Biological Supply) placed at 25 °C; fertilization should occur within 10–20 min, depending on sperm concentration.

steps.title: Concentrate embryos or larvae
steps.instruction: Pour the culture through a filter small enough to retain eggs/larvae (e.g., a 40 µm cell strainer, which captures particles < 80 µm).

steps.title: Transfer embryos/larvae to fresh dish
steps.instruction: Immediately immerse the filter containing embryos/larvae into a smaller glass dish filled with filtered seawater (FSW), then invert the filter to release the embryos/larvae, taking care to avoid air exposure.

steps.title: Incubate embryos/larvae
steps.instruction: Keep embryos and larvae at 25 °C in 4‑inch (or larger) glass culture dishes; change the water at least once per day to maintain health.

steps.title: Monitor developmental milestones
steps.instruction: Observe early cleavage a few hours post‑fertilization, blastula stage at 12–14 hpf, gastrulation by 24 hpf (when cilia begin beating and embryos swim), and active swimming planula larvae by 48 hpf.
